title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with meat, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet or scrambled egg with meat prepared without added fat is a dish made from eggs and lean meat (such as chicken breast or turkey). Eggs provide high‑quality protein, B‑vitamins and minerals, while the lean meat adds extra protein, iron and zinc.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most nutrient‑dense foods with a high biological value.
Cooking without added fat preserves the natural taste of the ingredients and reduces the calorie count.
Meat in the dish increases satiety and provides a slower release of energy.
Traditionally omelets are cooked with a little oil, but a non‑stick pan or steaming can be used to avoid added fat.
The dish is commonly included in the diets of athletes and people monitoring fat intake.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Eggs and lean meat together supply all essential amino acids, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain B12, riboflavin (B2) and biotin, while meat provides niacin (B3) and B6, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Meat adds iron and zinc; eggs contribute phosphorus and selenium, supporting immunity and bone health.

items.title: Low in added fats
items.content: The absence of added oil makes the dish suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The combination of protein and the small amount of natural fat in eggs helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Meat quality
items.content: Use lean, fresh meat without excessive salt or preservatives.

items.title: Spoilage
items.content: Fresh meat and eggs should be stored at ≤4 °C and used within a few days.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat the eggs, stir in finely chopped lean meat, season with salt and pepper. Pour the mixture onto a pre‑heated non‑stick pan with no oil, cook over medium heat, gently stirring until the eggs set but remain tender.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The omelet is best eaten fresh. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a pan without adding fat.
